transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Miles Ortega (Redwood SE), Evan Li (Northstar Head of Integrations), Priya Menon (Northstar Solutions Architect), Marco Rios (BizDev), Jules Park (Cloud Ops)

Auto-summary (auto):
Northstar Galaxy is a channel/reseller partner exploring a GPU onramp for their SaaS customers. Key asks: VPC/private onramp patterns, partner margins/marketplace flow, SOC2/KMS requirements, and a pilot performance run on A100/H100. Redwood AE+SE to send security pack and schedule benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- Partner GTM & reseller flow
- Technical integration: VPC peering, private deployment, dedicated pools, kernel compatibility
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Benchmarks and pilot scope: model variants, sequence lengths, throughput SLOs
- Commercial: margins, reserved capacity, marketplace listing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro — I'm Samira, I'm the AE working with partners. Miles is our solutions engineer here. How's everyone doing?
[00:11] Evan: Good, thanks. Hi Samira, hi Miles. Excited to get into this — we got a lot of interest from our telco customers.
[00:18] Priya: Yeah hi, thanks. We moved this earlier in the week, sorry running a bit behind.
[00:22] Miles: No worries. Quick agenda: high-level partner model, technical integration options (hosted API, dedicated, private), and then runbook for pilot + benchmarks.
[00:30] Marco: That's perfect. From our side we want to understand margins and how the marketplace or reseller flow looks.
[00:36] Jules: And I'm mostly interested in the network pattern — VPC peering vs private deploy — and cert rotation / KMS.
[00:43] Samira: Great. Quick overview of Redwood's partner programs: you can resell hosted API with partner margins, or co-manage dedicated pools, or onboard customers into private deployments if they need VPC/on-prem. We also support a marketplace listing where we handle billing.
[00:58] Evan: When you say dedicated pools — that's reserved GPU capacity we run for the partner's customers, right? Or is that on-prem?
[01:05] Miles: Good question. Dedicated is our reserved GPU pools in our infra — it's isolated by tenancy, predictable throughput. Private is the one you can run in your VPC or on-prem with a customer-controlled plane. There is also hybrid where we route by policy.
[01:20] Priya: For regulated customers we'll need a private option, ideally customer-managed keys and audit logs. Do you support HSM or bring-your-own-KMS?
[01:29] Miles: Yes, BYOK is supported — we integrate with major cloud KMS and HSM providers. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available via the console. There can be a lag depending on retention levels.
[01:37] Jules: How does network routing work for private? Is it a VPN, VPC peering, or do you run an agent?
[01:43] Miles: We have multiple patterns: VPC peering for cross-account, private link style endpoints for cloud regions, and an on-prem package that customers can run behind their firewall. For enterprise we often recommend VPC peering + restricted egress for better security.
[01:54] Evan: Any constraints around GPU types in private? Our customers sometimes require H100 for latency sensitive inference.
[02:00] Miles: On the private on-prem package we support CUDA-based stacks — A100 and H100 commonly. For hosted dedicated pools we already run both; it's a capacity/availability question. We'll propose a pilot with both so you can see perf differences.
[02:12] Marco: From a commercial angle, what's typical markup for partners on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:17] Samira: We have tiered margins — for marketplace/reseller flows it's X% (we agreed not to say exact on call), and for co-managed dedicated pools margins shift depending on commit length. We'll send a partner sheet after this call.
[02:30] Priya: About data residency — we have EU customers that need EU-only processing and log residency. Can you pin regions per customer?
[02:37] Miles: Yes, you can pin model serving regions. For private we can also deploy the control plane regionally. Note in some cases you need a private deployment to meet strict residency.
[02:47] Evan: Quick question on model variants — if a customer wants llama-type open model vs a tuned commercial model, is that flexible?
[02:55] Miles: Absolutely. Our model catalog includes open models and verified profiles; we also support customer's custom models in private deployments. There are quantization and kernel tradeoffs we can advise on.
[03:06] Jules: Do you provide tooling for batching and KV cache across multi-tenant workloads?
[03:11] Miles: Yes — runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache. For multi-tenant we have tenant isolation on caching and policies to avoid noisy neighbors. We can also recommend batch sizes based on latency targets.
[03:24] Priya: Earlier you mentioned tracing. We need per-request audit logs for compliance, and we'd like to tie logs back to our SSO identities.
[03:33] Samira: SSO/SAML is supported; you can map to RBAC in the console and we propagate identity for audit. We'll include the SSO config doc.
[03:42] Marco: How fast is onboarding from your side? We want a 60-day pilot to show tower customers. What's realistic?
[03:48] Samira: Typical is 2-6 weeks for a pilot depending on private vs hosted. Hosted is fastest; private with VPC or on-prem extends time for network approvals. For a 60-day pilot we recommend hosted/dedicated with a private option for one or two anchor customers.
[04:00] Evan: For the pilot benchmarks — what metrics do you capture? Tokens/sec, latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens?
[04:09] Miles: We'll capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization, and cost breakdown per token plus memory/KV metrics. We'll also produce a runbook with reproducible scripts.
[04:18] Priya: We have some internal prompt sets for telecom NLU — around 512 tokens average. Will that be okay?
[04:25] Miles: Perfect; we'll tailor the benchmark to 512 avg and some tail sequences up to 4k to exercise kv cache.
[04:32] Jules: Firewall question — do you require outbound connections from customer VPC to Redwood control plane?
[04:37] Miles: For private control plane there are minimal outbound endpoints for control, but inference can stay within the VPC if you use the on-prem runtime. We'll share a network diagram.
[04:46] Evan: On the reseller/marketplace mechanics: how does billing work if we list Redwood as an onramp? Customers buy via us or via your portal?
[04:55] Samira: We can do both. Marketplace listing means Redwood handles billing and you earn a margin. Reseller/co-sell can have partner-managed billing where we invoice you or we do net terms. We'll include templates.
[05:06] Marco: Any gotchas on support SLAs when we're reselling?
[05:10] Samira: There's a support matrix by partner tier; dedicated/reserved customers get higher SLOs. We'll include SLA tiers.
[05:16] Evan: Great. Can we talk briefly about security review — if our large customer runs a security questionnaire, do you have an existing pack?
[05:23] Miles: Yes — security pack includes SOC2 report, ISO where applicable, network diagrams, encryption at rest/in transit details, and sample contracts. We'll attach it.
[05:30] Priya: Are there any penetration test restrictions for private deployments? Customers sometimes want to run pentests.
[05:36] Miles: For private deployments where the runtime is customer-managed, pentests are under their control. For hosted/dedicated we have a pentest process and can coordinate. We'll share the policy.
[05:44] Marco: Pricing question — can we offer zero-day credits or promotional pricing for initial signups?
[05:49] Samira: Yes, we can provide promotional credits for pilot customers; for larger commitments we'll discuss reserved capacity pricing.
[05:55] Evan: Let's map stakeholders: Marco is primary for GTM/commercial, Priya will be technical lead for integration, Jules owns cloud ops / network, Evan is overall. Does that sound right?
[06:05] Priya: Yes.
[06:07] Marco: Yep.
[06:09] Miles: Cool. Quick technical deep dive: if you plan to route by cost vs latency, our smart routing can fall back to cheaper quantized variants during congestion. That might be useful for your multi-tenant SaaS customers.
[06:21] Priya: How does fallback affect model quality and state? If a conversation is mid-session, are you preserving KV cache when falling back?
[06:30] Miles: Good point. We preserve KV cache within compatible variants; fallback to a smaller quantized model may lose some fidelity. Our rollout policies let you define when to fall back and we can pin sessions to the same tier to avoid mid-request switches.
[06:44] Evan: For anchor customers with tight SLOs, we'd prefer no fallback — just queue or burst to reserved capacity?
[06:50] Miles: You can configure to never fallback for those customers, yes — that's what dedicated reserved pools are for.
[06:55] Samira: Quick interjection — Marco, can you share the rough scale (e.g., concurrent sessions, tokens/day) you expect for the first 6 months?
[07:03] Marco: Targeting 1000 concurrent sessions at peak for telecom pilot, maybe 10M tokens/day. But that's rough — we'll refine.
[07:11] Miles: That's helpful. We'll size the pilot accordingly; likely a small dedicated pool or high-capacity hosted plan.
[07:18] Priya: About telemetry — can we stream traces to our Splunk or Datadog?
[07:23] Miles: Yes, we can forward logs/traces; we have integrations for Datadog, Splunk, and also S3 log export.
[07:29] Jules: Any special kernel/compile constraints for H100? We run mixed workloads.
[07:34] Miles: On H100 we leverage newer attention kernels — we can advise quantization profiles. We also recommend specific CUDA/cuDNN versions; we'll send a compatibility matrix.
[07:44] Evan: For sales enablement, do you have partner-facing collateral? One-pagers, deck, pricing card?
[07:50] Samira: Yes — partner playbook, pitch deck, and a one-page pricing summary. I'll share.
[07:56] Priya: Is there an integration sandbox? We want to test end-to-end with a dev account and sample datasets.
[08:02] Miles: We'll provision a sandbox tenant for partners — includes limited dedicated capacity and test keys. Good for POC.
[08:09] Marco: For marketplace listing, what's the approval time? Can we be live before the pilot ends?
[08:15] Samira: Typically 2-3 weeks for listing review. For pilot we can do private listing for early customers.
[08:22] Evan: Are there co-marketing funds or commit-based incentives?
[08:26] Samira: We have co-marketing programs and MDF for strategic partners; that's stage-gated. We'll include program detail.
[08:33] Priya: Back to compliance: Do you support per-tenant data retention policies? Some customers need 7-day logs retention and others 365.
[08:41] Miles: Adjustable retention is supported in the console; for longer retention we may push logs to customer-owned storage.
[08:47] Jules: On the network diagram you mentioned sending — can you include the ports, CIDR ranges, and any required proxy config?
[08:54] Miles: Yes — we'll include a recommended firewall ruleset and proxy examples.
[09:00] Evan: Okay let's outline pilot scope: 6-week pilot, hosted + small dedicated pool, benchmark runs on A100 and H100, security review completed in parallel, and marketplace/reseller flow discussed.
[09:11] Samira: Sounds good. Miles — we'll need your benchmark plan.
[09:15] Miles: I'll draft a plan with datasets, seq lengths (512 avg, 4k tail), model variants (open model, quantized variant), and metrics. Propose 2 run windows so you can pick.
[09:25] Priya: We'll provide prompt sets and a list of anchor accounts.
[09:29] Marco: And we'll need a pricing tile for the pilot customers.
[09:33] Samira: We'll include a pricing proposal.
[09:36] Evan: Anything else on integration complexity? Priya: We're worried about session affinity and scaling spikes.
[09:43] Miles: Our autoscaling supports burst capacity and sticky routing. For real-time apps we recommend a combination of reserved capacity and burst to keep tail latency low.
[09:54] Samira: Quick pause — any blockers from your side to move forward?
[09:58] Priya: Network approvals will be the gating item for private deployments, but for hosted/dedicated we can move faster.
[10:05] Jules: Also procurement — need legal to review partner MSA, but that's standard.
[10:09] Samira: We'll send MSA template.
[10:12] Evan: Ok final recap?
[10:14] Samira: Recap: 1) Samira sends security pack, partner playbook, pricing tiles, and MSA template; 2) Miles sends benchmark plan and compatibility matrix; 3) Jules provides network constraints and schedule; 4) Northstar provides prompt sets and anchor customer list. We'll aim to schedule benchmark in the next week.
[10:33] Marco: Good.
[10:34] Priya: Works for me.
[10:35] Miles: One more quick note — there's small risk with quantization on hallucination rates for some NLU tasks; we'll include quality checks in the eval pipeline.
[10:45] Evan: Good call.
[10:47] Samira: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts by EOD Friday.
[10:52] Jules: Thanks all.
[10:54] Call ends.

Notes about transcription: occasional overlapping speech, some product names slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cache").
